note: Color & Tell hear scripts. Hear the story reads `hear` when present. Four beats: place, what happened, one KJV line, one big idea. Same Color door. Nothing uploads.

hear.creation:
It is the first morning of the world. Dark, then God speaks.
He made light, sky, land, living things, and people in His image.
“And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.” Genesis 1:31.
God made everything good — including you.
hear.david:
Two armies stand on the hills. A giant is shouting.
A shepherd boy named David comes with a sling, not armor. He runs in the name of the Lord.
“The battle is the LORD's.” 1 Samuel 17:47.
God is bigger than the loudest fear.
hear.jesus-children:
People are around Jesus. Families brought little children.
Some tried to send the children away. Jesus did not.
“Suffer the little children to come unto me.” Mark 10:14.
You can come to Jesus even with crayons in your hand.
hear.daniel-lions:
Night in a den of lions. Daniel is there because he would not stop praying.
God sent His angel. The lions did not hurt him.
“My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.” Daniel 6:22.
God is with you when you are afraid.
hear.empty-tomb:
Early morning. Women walk to a tomb.
The stone is rolled away. He is not here.
“He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.” Matthew 28:6.
Jesus is alive.
hear.baby-moses:
A river. Reeds. A small basket floating.
A mother hides her baby, a princess finds him, and God keeps him safe.
“She called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.” Exodus 2:10.
God watches over little ones.
hear.moses-red-sea:
A shore with water in front and an army behind.
Moses stretches out his hand. The sea opens. God’s people walk through on dry ground.
“Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.” Exodus 14:13.
God makes a way when there seems none.
hear.jonah:
A ship on a wild sea. Jonah is running from God.
A storm comes. A great fish swallows him. Then God gives him another chance.
“And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.” Jonah 2:10.
God’s mercy reaches farther than we run.
hear.noah:
A big boat on dry ground, before the rain.
Noah obeys. Animals come two by two. After the flood, God sets a bow in the cloud.
“And God remembered Noah.” Genesis 8:1.
God keeps His promises.
hear.feeding-5000:
A hillside. A hungry crowd. Almost no food.
A boy has five loaves and two fishes. Jesus gives thanks, and everyone eats.
“And they did all eat, and were filled.” Matthew 14:20.
Jesus provides more than enough.
hear.jesus-storm:
A boat at night. Waves come in.
Jesus is asleep. Then He stands and speaks to the wind.
“Peace, be still.” Mark 4:39.
Jesus is Lord over the storm.
hear.good-samaritan:
A dusty road. A man is hurt.
Some walk past. A stranger stops, binds the wounds, and pays for care.
“Go, and do thou likewise.” Luke 10:37.
Love your neighbor with real help.
hear.prodigal-son:
A road home. A son who spent everything.
He turns back sorry. His father runs, hugs him, and makes a feast.
“For this my son was dead, and is alive again.” Luke 15:24.
The Father runs to welcome home.
hear.walks-on-water:
A dark lake. The boat is far from land.
Jesus walks on the water. Peter comes, then looks at the wind, and Jesus catches him.
“Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.” Matthew 14:27.
Keep your eyes on Jesus.
hear.zacchaeus:
A tree beside the road. A short man climbs it.
Jesus looks up, calls his name, and goes to his house.
“For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.” Luke 19:10.
Jesus knows your name.
hear.woman-at-well:
A well at noon. Jesus sits, tired.
He asks a woman for water, then offers living water that never runs out.
“Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst.” John 4:14.
Jesus offers living water.
hear.ruth-naomi:
A dusty road between two homes.
Ruth will not leave Naomi. She says, your people will be my people, and your God my God.
“Whither thou goest, I will go.” Ruth 1:16.
Loyal love is a quiet strength.
hear.lazarus:
A tomb with a stone. Friends are crying.
Jesus weeps. Then He calls, Lazarus, come forth, and the dead man walks out.
“I am the resurrection, and the life.” John 11:25.
Jesus’ word brings life.
hear.lost-sheep:
A hillside. Ninety-nine sheep safe. One is missing.
The shepherd goes after the one, finds it, and carries it home glad.
“Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.” Luke 15:6.
The Shepherd comes for the one.
hear.jairus-daughter:
A quiet house. People say a little girl is dead.
Jesus takes her hand and speaks.
“Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.” Mark 5:41.
Jesus’ word brings life.
hear.blind-man:
A roadside. A man who cannot see.
Jesus makes clay, sends him to wash, and he comes seeing.
“Lord, I believe.” John 9:38.
Jesus opens eyes and hearts.
hear.fishers-of-men:
The sea of Galilee. Nets in the water.
Jesus calls Peter and Andrew from their work.
“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Matthew 4:19.
Jesus calls ordinary people.
hear.wedding-cana:
A wedding feast. The wine is gone.
Jesus tells them to fill waterpots. The water becomes wine.
“This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee.” John 2:11.
Jesus turns need into joy.
hear.mustard-seed:
A tiny seed in a field.
It is the least of seeds, then it grows into a tree.
“The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed.” Matthew 13:31.
Small faith can grow.
hear.the-sower:
A farmer walking, throwing seed.
Some seed is eaten, some dries, some is choked, some grows.
“He that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it.” Matthew 13:23.
God’s Word wants good soil.
hear.triumphal-entry:
A road into Jerusalem. Coats and branches on the ground.
Jesus comes gentle, on a donkey. People shout Hosanna.
“Hosanna to the son of David.” Matthew 21:9.
The King comes in peace.
hear.lost-coin:
A dark house. One coin is missing.
A woman lights a candle, sweeps, and seeks until she finds it.
“Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.” Luke 15:9.
Heaven rejoices when the lost is found.
hear.healing-paralytic:
A crowded house. Friends lower a mat through the roof.
Jesus forgives the man, then tells him to take up his bed and walk.
“Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.” Matthew 9:2.
Jesus forgives and heals.
hear.good-shepherd:
Green pasture. A shepherd with his sheep.
Jesus says He is the good shepherd, and He gives His life for the sheep.
“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.” John 10:11.
The Good Shepherd knows His sheep.
hear.feeding-4000:
Another hillside. Another hungry crowd.
Jesus has compassion. Seven loaves and a few fishes, and all eat.
“And they did all eat, and were filled.” Matthew 15:37.
Jesus cares for hungry hearts.
hear.wise-foolish-builders:
Two houses. Rain is coming.
One is built on rock and stands. One is built on sand and falls.
“Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.” Matthew 7:24.
Build your life on His words.
hear.the-talents:
A master going on a journey. Bags of money in servants’ hands.
Two use what they were given. One hides his in the earth.
“Well done, thou good and faithful servant.” Matthew 25:21.
Faithful with a little matters.
hear.persistent-widow:
A judge’s door. A widow keeps knocking.
She will not stop asking until he helps her.
“Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.” Luke 18:1.
Keep praying. Do not faint.
hear.healing-leper:
A man kneels in the road.
He says, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean. Jesus touches him.
“I will; be thou clean.” Mark 1:41.
Jesus is willing to make clean.
hear.joseph-coat:
A bright coat. Angry brothers.
They sell Joseph away, but God is with him still.
“But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.” Genesis 50:20.
God can use hard days for good.
hear.joseph-dreams:
A prison. Then a palace.
Joseph says dreams belong to God, and God uses him to save many lives.
“It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.” Genesis 41:16.
God can turn sorrow into saving.
hear.burning-bush:
A mountain. A bush on fire that does not burn up.
God calls Moses by name and sends him to help His people.
“I AM THAT I AM.” Exodus 3:14.
God sees. God sends.
hear.jericho:
A city with high walls.
God’s people walk around it in quiet obedience. Then the walls fall.
“The wall fell down flat.” Joshua 6:20.
God keeps His word.
hear.gideon-fleece:
A threshing floor at night. A fleece on the ground.
Gideon asks God to make it sure. God is patient, then gives the victory.
“The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.” Judges 6:12.
God can use a small yes.
hear.samson:
A strong man. A gift from God.
Samson’s strength was not his own. When he called on the Lord again, God heard.
“And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him.” Judges 14:6.
Strength is a gift to use for God.
hear.esther:
A palace hall. A young woman is afraid, and still she goes in.
She fasts, then speaks for her people.
“If I perish, I perish.” Esther 4:16.
God can give quiet courage.
hear.fiery-furnace:
A hot furnace. Three friends will not bow.
A fourth is seen with them in the fire, and they come out unhurt.
“Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us.” Daniel 3:17.
God can keep you in the fire.
hear.abraham-isaac:
A mountain path. A father and his boy.
Abraham trusts God. God provides a ram, and Isaac lives.
“God will provide himself a lamb.” Genesis 22:8.
God will provide.
hear.elijah-carmel:
A mountain. Two altars. A waiting crowd.
Baal is silent. Elijah prays, and the fire of the LORD falls.
“The LORD, he is the God.” 1 Kings 18:39.
The LORD, He is the God.
hear.naaman:
A river. A proud captain with sick skin.
He almost will not dip. Then he obeys, and God makes him clean.
“His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child.” 2 Kings 5:14.
Humble obedience meets mercy.
hear.boy-samuel:
A quiet temple room at night.
God calls a boy by name. Samuel learns to say, Speak, Lord.
“Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.” 1 Samuel 3:9.
God still speaks. We can listen.
hear.ten-lepers:
A road. Ten sick men cry for mercy.
Jesus heals them. Only one turns back to say thank you.
“Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?” Luke 17:17.
Come back and give thanks.
hear.pharisee-tax-collector:
The temple. Two men praying.
One talks about himself. One says, God be merciful to me a sinner.
“God be merciful to me a sinner.” Luke 18:13.
Humble hearts are heard.
hear.widows-mite:
The temple treasury. Coins dropping in.
Rich people give from extra. A poor widow gives two small mites, all she had.
“She of her want did cast in all that she had.” Mark 12:44.
God sees what it cost.
hear.centurion-servant:
A house nearby. A servant is sick.
A soldier says Jesus does not even have to come inside. Speak the word only.
“Speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.” Matthew 8:8.
Great faith trusts Jesus’ word.
hear.abraham-sarah:
A tent under the stars. Two old people wait.
God promised a son. Sarah laughs. Then Isaac is born.
“Is any thing too hard for the LORD?” Genesis 18:14.
Nothing is too hard for the Lord.
hear.elisha-oil:
A small house. Empty jars.
A widow pours from a little oil, and it keeps filling until the jars are full.
“Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.” 2 Kings 4:3.
God’s jar does not fail.
hear.hannah-samuel:
The temple. A woman praying with no voice, only moving lips.
Hannah asks God for a child. God hears. She names him Samuel.
“For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition.” 1 Samuel 1:27.
God hears a poured-out soul.
hear.david-jonathan:
A field. Two friends.
Jonathan loves David as his own soul and gives him his robe and his sword.
“The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.” 1 Samuel 18:1.
True friendship is loyal.
hear.rich-young-ruler:
A road. A young man with many things.
He asks Jesus about eternal life, then goes away sad, because his stuff still held his heart.
“Come and follow me.” Matthew 19:21.
Follow Jesus above all.
hear.pearl-great-price:
A merchant looking at pearls.
He finds one of great price, and sells all he has to buy it.
“The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls.” Matthew 13:45.
The kingdom is worth everything.
hear.withered-hand:
A synagogue. A man with a stiff, withered hand.
Some watch to accuse. Jesus says, Stretch forth thine hand, and it is made whole.
“Stretch forth thine hand.” Matthew 12:13.
Jesus restores what is broken.
hear.unforgiving-servant:
A king’s court. A huge debt is forgiven.
That same servant chokes a man who owed him a little.
“Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant?” Matthew 18:33.
Forgiven people forgive.
hear.boy-david:
A field of sheep. Brothers who look tall and strong.
God does not choose the way people choose. He sends for the youngest, keeping sheep.
“The LORD looketh on the heart.” 1 Samuel 16:7.
God looks on the heart.
hear.elijah-ravens:
A hidden brook. A prophet waiting.
Ravens bring bread and flesh morning and night.
“I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.” 1 Kings 17:4.
God provides in quiet ways.
hear.writing-on-wall:
A loud feast. Gold cups from God’s house.
A hand writes on the wall. God has weighed the king, and found him wanting.
“Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.” Daniel 5:27.
God weighs the heart.
hear.ruth-boaz:
A barley field at harvest.
Ruth gleans. Boaz is kind. God opens a future of hope.
“The LORD recompense thy work.” Ruth 2:12.
Kindness opens a future of hope.
hear.jesus-baptism:
A river. Crowds, then Jesus stepping in.
The Spirit comes like a dove. A voice from heaven speaks.
“This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” Matthew 3:17.
This is My beloved Son.
hear.emmaus-road:
A long road after a sad weekend.
A stranger walks with two friends, opens the Scriptures, and they know Him in the breaking of bread.
“Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?” Luke 24:32.
Jesus walks with us and opens the Word.
hear.jesus-washes-feet:
An upper room. A basin of water.
Jesus, their Lord, kneels and washes the disciples’ feet.
“If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.” John 13:14.
The greatest serves.
hear.transfiguration:
A high mountain. Three friends watching.
Jesus’ face shines like the sun. A voice from the cloud says, Hear Him.
“This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.” Matthew 17:5.
Listen to Him.
hear.jordan-crossing:
A river at flood. Priests holding the ark.
When their feet touch the water, God makes dry ground, and the people pass over.
“The priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan.” Joshua 3:17.
God keeps His promise into the land.
hear.balaams-donkey:
A narrow path. An angel in the way.
A donkey sees what the prophet does not, and God opens her mouth to warn him.
“The LORD opened the mouth of the ass.” Numbers 22:28.
God can warn in unexpected ways.
hear.elijah-taken-up:
A road with two prophets walking.
A chariot of fire, a whirlwind, and Elijah is taken up. Elisha sees it.
“There appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire… and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.” 2 Kings 2:11.
God receives His faithful servant.
hear.nehemiah-walls:
Broken walls. Burned gates.
Nehemiah prays, then builds with a tool in one hand and a watch in the other.
“So built we the wall… for the people had a mind to work.” Nehemiah 4:6.
Build with prayer and courage.
hear.jesus-tempted:
A wilderness. Forty days. Hunger.
The tempter comes with If thou be the Son. Jesus answers with Scripture.
“It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” Matthew 4:4.
Answer temptation with God’s Word.
hear.paul-silas-prison:
A prison at midnight. Feet in stocks.
Paul and Silas pray and sing. An earthquake opens doors. A jailer asks how to be saved.
“Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.” Acts 16:31.
Praise can rise even in chains.
hear.lydia-purple:
A riverbank on the sabbath. Women praying.
Lydia hears, and the Lord opens her heart. She is baptized, and her house.
“Whose heart the Lord opened.” Acts 16:14.
The Lord opens hearts to believe.
hear.tabitha-dorcas:
An upper room. Coats sewn with love.
Tabitha had died. Peter prays, and she sits up alive.
“Tabitha, arise.” Acts 9:40.
Kind deeds matter to God.
hear.nativity:
A small town at night. No room in the inn.
A baby is laid in a manger. Angels tell shepherds, A Saviour is born.
“For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.” Luke 2:11.
Jesus, our Saviour, is born.
hear.paul-shipwreck:
A breaking ship. A long storm.
God promised Paul that all would live. They reach land on boards and broken pieces.
“And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.” Acts 27:44.
God keeps His word in the storm.
hear.rahab-spies:
A house on a city wall. A scarlet line in the window.
Rahab hides two spies and trusts the God of Israel.
“The LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.” Joshua 2:11.
Faith can shelter God’s people.
hear.elijah-widow:
A city gate. A widow gathering sticks.
Elijah asks for a little cake first. The barrel of meal does not waste.
“The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail.” 1 Kings 17:14.
God’s jar does not fail.
hear.philip-ethiopian:
A chariot on a desert road. A man reading Isaiah.
Philip runs near, begins at that scripture, and preaches Jesus. They find water.
“Understandest thou what thou readest?” Acts 8:30.
Scripture leads to Jesus.
hear.david-spares-saul:
A cave. The king is close enough to hurt.
David cuts a piece of Saul’s robe, then will not put forth his hand against him.
“The LORD judge between me and thee… but mine hand shall not be upon thee.” 1 Samuel 24:12.
Mercy is stronger than revenge.
hear.ll-honesty:
A quiet table. Words about to come out.
God delights in those who deal truly. A soft, true word is a kind of love.
“Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.” Proverbs 12:22.
Truth is a kind of love.
hear.ll-commandments:
Two steps for a whole life.
Love God with all your heart. Love your neighbor as yourself.
“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart… Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” Matthew 22:37-39.
Love God. Love your neighbor.
